questions.text: Which vegetable are you most likely to cry over when chopping it?
questions.explanation: Onions release a gas that irritates the eyes.

questions.text: Which dairy product is made by churning cream?
What is the main ingredient of guacamole?
questions.explanation: Guacamole is a mashed avocado dip from Mexico.

questions.text: Which Italian cheese is traditionally used on a Margherita pizza?
questions.explanation: Mozzarella, tomato and basil mirror the Italian flag.

questions.text: Which fermented soybean paste is the key ingredient of a traditional Japanese soup?
questions.explanation: Miso soup is made by dissolving fermented soybean paste in stock.

questions.text: Which fresh Indian cheese is made by curdling milk and pressing the curds into blocks?
questions.explanation: Paneer is an unaged, non-melting cheese widely used in Indian cooking.

questions.text: Which French phrase means everything in its place, referring to preparing ingredients before cooking?
questions.explanation: Mise en place is a core kitchen discipline.

questions.text: Which green paste is the usual accompaniment to sushi?
questions.explanation: Wasabi is a pungent Japanese horseradish paste.

questions.text: Which grain is polenta traditionally made from?
questions.explanation: Polenta is boiled cornmeal from northern Italy.

questions.text: Which classic French white sauce is made from butter, flour and milk?
questions.explanation: Bechamel is one of the five French mother sauces.

questions.text: Which Italian rice dish is cooked by gradually adding hot stock?
questions.explanation: Risotto uses starchy rice like arborio.

questions.text: Which gas makes bread dough rise?
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugars and releases carbon dioxide.

questions.text: Which Spanish cold soup is made from tomatoes, peppers and cucumber?
In French cooking, what is a roux?
questions.explanation: A roux is used to thicken sauces and soups.

questions.text: What does the Italian cooking term al dente literally mean?
questions.explanation: Al dente pasta is cooked but still firm to the bite.

spares.text: Which fruit is dried to make raisins?
Which crescent-shaped French pastry is a breakfast staple?
spares.explanation: Croissants are made from laminated yeast dough.

spares.text: Which cooking term means briefly boiling food, then plunging it into iced water?
spares.explanation: Blanching halts cooking and fixes colour.
